requirements.requirement: /tmp mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev, persistent via fstab
requirements.summary: Baseline showed /tmp was not a separate mount and had no fstab entry (cmd-dc7db08cdec14666, cmd-9a00c9985ef242ff, cmd-ec5e144b07fa42a5). Executor added a tmpfs /tmp entry to /etc/fstab with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime (cmd-cc6932c629c7439b), mounted it live (cmd-50d12e707873458d), and functionally confirmed script execution denied (exit 126), setuid execution denied, and device-node open denied on /tmp both before reboot (cmd-58a25c08420b4986, cmd-a977ad90d80149f3, cmd-86b50fdebb244eb4) and after an actual reboot (cmd-a6e7db4b5fd14284, cmd-1f56d41260724033).

requirements.requirement: /dev/shm mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev, persistent via fstab
requirements.summary: Baseline showed /dev/shm was already tmpfs with nosuid,nodev,noexec live but had no fstab entry to persist those options (cmd-dc7db08cdec14666, cmd-ec5e144b07fa42a5). Executor added a matching fstab entry and remounted (cmd-cc6932c629c7439b, cmd-50d12e707873458d), then functionally verified setuid-binary execution denied on /dev/shm both pre-reboot (cmd-a977ad90d80149f3) and post-reboot (cmd-1f56d41260724033), with live mount options and fstab entry both confirmed present after reboot (cmd-a6e7db4b5fd14284).

Executor captured a pre-reboot boot_id (f3e63865...) and healthy dual-mount state (cmd-f39b3a354ef74c9c), issued a real reboot (cmd-3ae82af7364741e8), observed the node unreachable through multiple poll attempts during the transition (cmd-e388e06de98f4003 through cmd-cc8ab7533051449c), then confirmed a new boot_id (ca0d1bc4...) with uptime 0 (cmd-825737f5a9b14da1), and re-verified both fstab and live mount options plus functional enforcement of noexec/nosuid/nodev post-reboot (cmd-a6e7db4b5fd14284, cmd-1f56d41260724033). This directly demonstrates the required transition (healthy baseline → bounded disruption → restoration → recovered, persisted state), corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 were configured with noexec,nosuid,nodev via persistent /etc/fstab tmpfs entries, applied live, and functionally verified to deny execution, setuid execution, and device-node access both before and after a genuine reboot (confirmed by a changed boot_id and corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots). Operational hygiene is good: all verification test artifacts were cleaned up, and the only mutations were directly tied to implementing or proving the required hardening and its persistence.
limitations: The pre-existing /tmp/builder.log was lost when /tmp was converted to a tmpfs mount; this is an inherent consequence of the required change rather than executor carelessness, but is noted for completeness.

systemctl/failed-services checks were unsupported on this Alpine (OpenRC) node, so failed-service state could not be directly cross-checked via that lifecycle observation; however, this does not affect the mount-hardening or reboot-persistence outcomes, which were verified through other direct evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to the task: fstab backup+edit (cmd-cc6932c629c7439b) and live mount/remount (cmd-50d12e707873458d) implement the hardening; the actual reboot (cmd-3ae82af7364741e8) is required to prove the 'survive a reboot' outcome, not an extraneous mutation. Functional-test artifacts created during verification (/tmp/t.sh, /tmp/testdev, /dev/shm/bb in cmd-58a25c08420b4986/cmd-a977ad90d80149f3, and /tmp/t2.sh, /dev/shm/bb2, /tmp/testdev2 in cmd-1f56d41260724033) were all removed within the same or immediately following command (cmd-86b50fdebb244eb4 and the rm at the end of cmd-1f56d41260724033), leaving no residue. One incidental side effect: converting /tmp to a tmpfs mount wiped the pre-existing /tmp/builder.log (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff), but this is an unavoidable consequence of the required mount change rather than an unnecessary or careless mutation by the executor.
